proposals: The Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying should publish an annual estimate of milk utilisation by product — liquid milk, ghee, paneer, curd, powder and cheese — split between organised and informal channels, so the 40%, 25% and roughly 35% processed-share figures in circulation are replaced by one official number.

The National Centre for Cold-Chain Development should publish a dated, state-wise cold-chain gap assessment stating its baseline and demand assumptions, so the gap is not quoted anywhere from roughly 8 million to 35 million tonnes depending on the source.

The Department of Commerce should host the full India–EFTA TEPA tariff schedules, line by line, in an accessible format on its own website, so whether ghee, paneer, butter and milk powder are excluded can be confirmed from the treaty text rather than from secondary summaries.

The Ministry of Food Processing Industries should publish, for mozzarella and other dairy products supported under the PLI scheme, the capacity added and output achieved by each beneficiary, so claims about capacity growth, such as the misattributed 1,200% figure, can be checked against official data.
